headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: ctx can observe Claude Code events and Perplexity can ingest uploaded content and web context, creating a plausible cross-agent trust path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs through a shared event channel. Perplexity is a browser/search agent that can surface untrusted web content. The pair therefore has a plausible instruction-hijack path even without a documented direct bridge; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ctx consumes Claude Code event payloads as instructions without provenance checks
IF Perplexity output is copied into ctx-managed prompts or hooks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all cross-agent text before reuse
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from event logs
Require a human review step before reusing Perplexity output
Restrict ctx hooks to metadata-only fields
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context. If the pair shares files or copied outputs, sensitive material can flow from ctx-managed artifacts into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted backend. The profiles do not show a guaranteed shared workspace, so this is not high, but the leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF ctx-managed logs or graph data are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity
IF Perplexity is used on documents containing audit/runtime logs or MCP server details
mitigations: Do not upload logs or graph exports to Perplexity
Redact identifiers before any copy-paste
Use a separate workspace for sensitive ctx artifacts
Turn off sharing of generated answers outside the operator
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads and clipboard

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while Perplexity can run browsers but cannot write the filesystem, execute shell, or modify git state. That limits direct write-write conflict. The main overlap is browser activity and shared session context, which can cause interference but not the high-severity mutable-resource collision described in the rubric.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same browser profile or session
IF ctx automation assumes exclusive control of browser state
mitigations: Use separate browser profiles per agent
Avoid concurrent browser automation on the same account
Serialize tasks that depend on browser state
Keep Perplexity read-only for shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared browser sessions

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is explicitly an observer of Claude Code events, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, which can be treated as authoritative by a second agent. The pair therefore supports an A-to-B trust chain with no documented verification step, creating a realistic cascading-error pathway in default use.
conditions: IF ctx-generated summaries are fed into Perplexity prompts
IF Perplexity answers are acted on without independent verification
mitigations: Require source checking before acting on either agent’s output
Keep a human in the loop for any factual claims
Separate drafting from execution roles
Mark Perplexity answers as untrusted until verified
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data. If those ctx artifacts contain regulated or internal data, sending them to Perplexity can create a residency/retention mismatch. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF ctx artifacts include regulated data or internal audit logs
IF those artifacts are uploaded to Perplexity without an approved DPA or retention review
mitigations: Classify ctx artifacts before sharing
Block uploads of regulated data to Perplexity
Use a compliant tenant or approved DPA
Delete uploaded files after use
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
